question.text: 'Indus Parallel Structure AIF' has domestic and Mauritius offshore pools. The IM in India enters into an Investment Advisory Arrangement with the Mauritius fund. Which of the following MUST the advisory arrangement satisfy to avoid POEM / Indian permanent establishment concerns?

answer.text: Advisory must be binding on the offshore fund
Advisory must be NON-BINDING and restricted in scope; offshore fund retains independent decision-making
Advisory must be executed with a 5-year lock-in
Advisory must be billed at USD 1 flat fee

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.5.3 and 8.5.1: to prevent the Indian office being characterised as a POEM / PE of the offshore fund, advisory must be NON-BINDING and the offshore fund retains independent decision-making. Binding advice collapses the structure. The Trap: Option A is the exact trigger for POEM risk. Option C fabricates. Option D confuses with feeder fund symbolic fee. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the non-binding carve-out. XVI (Tax) tests POEM consequences more broadly. Manager's Pro-Tip: Ensure board minutes of the offshore fund show independent deliberation on each investment, with the Indian advice listed as one input. This paper trail is your primary POEM defence in an enquiry.
